items.title: Two men, including disabled mechanic, charged over Second Link race
items.summary: KULAI: Two mechanics, including a disabled man, were charged in the magistrate's court here today with reckless and dangerous driving during an alleged illegal race on the Johor Second Link expressway last Saturday. Mohamad Riduan Abd Ghani, 26, and Muhamad Aiman Izzuddin Shukri, 26, pleaded not guilty to the separate charges before Magistrate R. Salini. Amarpreet Singh and Abd Rahim Ali respectively.

items.title: Wireman escapes mandatory life term after court acquits him over cannabis cultivation charge
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 27 — A wireman escaped a possible life imprisonment after he was acquitted and discharged by the Sessions Court here today of a charge of allowing a cannabis plant to be cultivated at his home three years ago. Aszizi Ayub, 37, was cleared of the charge at the close of the prosecution’s case after the court found that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against him. “The court finds that the prosecution has failed to prove the case against the accused,” he said.

items.title: CIMB advances tokenised sukuk push with RM1.68bil pilot
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd, through CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, has completed a pilot to test the settlement of tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits in a controlled environment. The pilot involved a RM1.68 billion issuance under CIMB Islamic's existing RM10 billion senior sukuk wakalah programme, with tenures ranging from five to 15 years. Tokenisation allows financial assets such as sukuk to be represented digitally using distributed ledger technology, while tokenised deposits represent commercial bank money in digital form.

items.title: Man admits assaulting elderly neighbour with metal rod
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 62-year-old man today admitted in the Sessions Court here to assaulting his 86-year-old neighbour with a metal rod, leaving him seriously injured. Ooi Hock Wah pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 326 of the Penal Code before Sessions Court Judge Irwan Suainbon. The court was told that the victim, Oung Kien Hock, remained hospitalised and was still receiving treatment.

items.title: Factory operator claims trial over alleged rape, unnatural sex involving polytechnic student
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: A 22-year-old factory operator claimed trial at the Sessions Court today to raping and committing an unnatural sex act against a polytechnic student. The charge, under Section 376(1) of the Penal Code, carries a maximum 20-year jail term and whipping upon conviction. Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Izad Firdaus prosecuted while lawyer RSN Rayer represented the accused.

items.title: Rare sight at KL court as Najib, Muhyiddin and Ismail Sabri appear for separate cases
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Kuala Lumpur Court Complex today saw the rare simultaneous appearance of three former prime ministers, each attending separate court hearings. Former Prime Minister, Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin after arriving at the Kuala Lumpur High Court Complex. Among the currencies allegedly not declared were RM14.7 million, S$6 million, US$1.46 million, three million Swiss francs, €12.2 million, ¥363 million, £50,250, NZ$44,600, 34.8 million dirhams and A$352,850.

items.title: Three friends, born in 1957, reunited for Merdeka
items.summary: TUMPAT: For three former teachers, Merdeka celebrations carry a special meaning as they were all born in the same historic year — 1957. Wan Ahmad Khairuddin, a former teacher at SMK Berangan, was born on Sept 10, 1957, while Mat Salleh, who taught at SMK A Falahiah, was born on Jan 14 the same year. Zulkifli, a former teacher at SMK Tok Uban, was born on Nov 3, 1957.

items.title: Nepal floods: 55 Malaysians uncontactable, no casualties confirmed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Ministry has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties following devastating floods in Nepal's Rasuwa district. "At this stage, the ministry has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties," it said in a statement today. However, 55 Malaysian nationals reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu are currently uncontactable following floods triggered by the overflowing Bhote Koshi River on Aug 26.

items.title: The Times frontman recalls last conversation with late guitarist, urges dashcam witnesses to come forward
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Naza Mohamad, the frontman of local indie band The Times, is urging those with dashcam footage of a recent hit-and-run involving their late guitarist to come forward to assist with the police investigation. Speaking to local media during the 2 Konsert 2 Generasi press conference in KL yesterday, Naza revealed that their former bandmate Nazreen Sharkawi, 51, passed away on Aug 24 at Miri General Hospital, four days after falling into a coma following a hit-and-run accident in Miri, Sarawak. If anyone in Miri has dashcam footage, please share it.

items.title: Trial for accused mastermind of 9/11 attacks set for June 2028
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A US Air Force judge on Wednesday ordered Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, the accused mastermind of the Sept 11, 2001, attacks on the United States, and three co-defendants to go on trial before a military tribunal in June 2028. The trial-scheduling order entered by Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Michael Schrama marked the latest milestone in a military prosecution beset by two decades of legal deadlock surrounding the four detainees held in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba. Under Schrama's 11-page order, Mohammed and three co-defendants — Walid Muhammad Salih Mubarak bin 'Atash, Mustafa Ahmed Adam al Hawsawi, and Ali Abdul Aziz Ali — will stand trial starting on June 5, 2028.

items.title: Ismail Sabri leaves court after son posts RM300,000 bail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob has left the court complex after his son posted RM300,000 bail for him. Asked if he was in good health, Ismail Sabri replied: "Yes." Also seen were former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin and former Pahang Menteri Besar Tan Sri Adnan Yaakob.

items.title: Apparel group EMPG one step closer to Bursa listing, plans 15 new boutiques in two years
items.summary: The proposed IPO comprises a public issue of 121.6 million new shares and an offer for sale of 48.5 million existing shares. Of the new shares, 30.3 million, or about five per cent of the enlarged issued share capital, will be offered to the public via balloting, with half reserved for Bumiputera public investors. A total of 11.25 million shares, or 1.86 per cent, will be offered via private placement to selected investors.

items.title: Puchong residents saddled with infrastructure challenges
items.summary: DEVELOPMENT has transformed Puchong beyond recognition. A journey from Puchong Jaya to Sunway that should take five or 10 minutes can easily stretch to 40 minutes or an hour. The problem is compounded by Puchong's location.

items.title: Malaysia's business confidence rebounds sharply in Q3
items.summary: • Industry: 8.2 per cent, up from -3.7 per cent • Services: 5.2 per cent compared with 6.2 per cent • Construction: 4.1 per cent, up from -9.5 per cent • Wholesale & Retail Trade: 1.2 per cent, up from -7.5 per cent The department said the broad-based improvement reflects greater confidence in both domestic and external economic activity. Other states with positive readings included Pahang (7.1 per cent), Selangor (5.8 per cent), Sarawak (5.8 per cent) Perlis (5.4 per cent), Kedah (5.1 per cent), Pulau Pinang (5.0 per cent), Johor (4.9 per cent), Sabah (3.7 per cent), Kelantan (2.1 per cent) and Perak (1.5 per cent). Putrajaya registered 0.6 per cent.

items.title: Yayoi Kusama: Japan's kaleidoscopic, troubled 'polka dot queen'
items.summary: TOKYO: The dotty pumpkins and kaleidoscope rooms of Yayoi Kusama, who has died aged 97, were as vibrant as the artist herself, but her exuberant work was the expression of a long battle with mental illness. Once a fixture of the 1960s pop and minimalist scenes in New York, Japan's "polka dot queen" found huge commercial success in her later decades. Born in 1929, the youngest daughter of a wealthy but troubled family, Kusama began producing her signature dot and net patterns aged 10.

items.title: ‘Was there an invitation?’ Anwar questions Azmin’s claim he was invited back to PKR
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today appeared to question whether former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali was among the former party leaders and reformists he had invited to return to the party. Anwar was responding to a question about Azmin’s decision not to rejoin PKR following his recent call for veterans or “otai Reformasi” to return to the party. Anwar, who is also PKR president, had recently said the party’s doors remained open to former leaders and reformists who wanted to return and contribute to its reform agenda.

items.title: Mydin halts sale of Jalur Gemilang-themed tudung over star design error
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mydin has ordered all its outlets to immediately stop selling a Jalur Gemilang-themed tudung after a customer flagged an apparent error in its 14-point star design. Mydin said the error was caused by a printing mistake by its supplier, adding that it was taking action to prevent a recurrence. The user said the star design could be perceived as disrespectful to the Jalur Gemilang and questioned the retailer's checks before the product was placed on sale.

items.title: Anwar orders National Security Council, Nadma and Foreign Ministry to step up aid for Malaysians in India, Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the National Security Council (MKN), National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and Foreign Ministry to immediately coordinate efforts to assist Malaysians affected by the situation in India and Nepal. Anwar said he had instructed the relevant agencies to identify and contact Malaysian diplomatic missions in both countries to expedite assistance. “I have instructed all relevant departments, including the National Security Council (MKN) and the Foreign Ministry, to immediately identify and contact our ministries and embassies in both India and Nepal to expedite efforts to assist them,” he told reporters after launching the National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo (Nice 2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here.

items.title: Amir Hamzah on shaping Malaysia's next-gen financial system
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's next-generation financial system must balance innovation with trust, efficiency, resilience and stability as emerging technologies reshape the sector, said Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. The Finance Minister II said technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure and tokenisation would create new opportunities for the financial and capital markets. Amir Hamzah said Malaysia must therefore build a financial system that is more efficient, connected and inclusive, while strengthening the country's competitiveness and supporting future economic growth.

items.title: 17 Malaysians travelling together with Nepal agency remain uncontactable
items.summary: Fishtail Tours & Travels representative Roshan Panday said the group was travelling together and was last known to be near Timure, close to the Nepal-China border. He said an agency colleague last contacted one of the group members at 8.18am local time as they approached the border. ""They were travelling together.

items.title: Khaled: Don't boycott National Day celebrations over Rohingya issue
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The public should not boycott National Day celebrations over sentiments surrounding the Rohingya issue, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. He said Independence Day celebrations should not be driven by emotions or sentiments over specific issues affecting the country. Khaled also urged Malaysians to use this year's celebrations as an opportunity to reaffirm their commitment to safeguarding the country's sovereignty.

items.title: Anwar urges Malaysia’s tech sector to innovate without losing sight of values
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia must pursue advances in science, technology and artificial intelligence without losing sight of its values, culture and humanity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today. Speaking at the launch of the National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo (Nice 2026) at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here, Anwar said Malaysia’s pursuit of new technologies should remain grounded in the needs and interests of the people. “As emphasised by the Ministry and in the Malaysia Plan, we say that it should not only be ‘Made in Malaysia’, but also ‘Made by Malaysia’,” he said.

items.summary: IPOH: A wireman was acquitted and discharged by the Sessions Court here today of a charge of allowing a cannabis plant to be cultivated at his home three years ago. items.title: Malaysia to lead Asean green jobs agenda for 2026-2030
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia will continue to lead Asean's green jobs agenda for 2026-2030 after being entrusted with regional projects under the Asean Labour Ministers' new work programme. We must ensure the Asean workforce has the skills needed to fill new jobs. Ramanan said Malaysia had delivered two key green jobs documents under its 2025 Asean Chairmanship: the Asean Framework and Action Plan (FAP) for a Just and Inclusive Transition to Green Jobs 2025-2030 and the Joint Statement on an Actionable Plan for Green Jobs Towards a Sustainable and Inclusive Asean Workforce.

items.title: SoftBank in talks to buy stake in 1X at US$bil valuation
items.summary: Reuters could not immediately confirm the report. SoftBank Group and 1X did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. The 1X deal builds on SoftBank's broader push into robotics, following its agreement last year to acquire Swiss engineering group ABB's robotics business for US$5.4 billion.

items.title: Army ready to assist in flood-hit Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Armed Forces are ready to contribute their expertise and capabilities to a humanitarian mission in flood-hit Nepal if called upon. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the armed forces were prepared to assist should the government decide that their capabilities were needed for the humanitarian response. As we have stated, one of the things that the armed forces can contribute is in terms of humanitarian missions.

items.title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for US$12.9bil
items.summary: MEXICO CITY: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face, a repository of open-source AI models, for US$12.9 billion, The Information reported on Wednesday, citing a person with knowledge of the deal. Nvidia was among companies such as Salesforce and Alphabet's Google that backed Hugging Face in a US$235 million funding round in 2023, valuing the company at US$4.5 billion. In January, the Financial Times reported that Hugging Face rejected a US$500 million investment offer from Nvidia last year that would have valued it at US$7 billion.

items.title: Japan's Nikkei reverses early gains as Nvidia supplier Advantest falls
items.summary: The Nikkei was down 0.14 per cent at 66,170.13, as of 0204 GMT, while the broader Topix rose 0.19 per cent to 4,118.69. Advantest was last down 1.96 per cent. Technology investor SoftBank Group eased 0.56 per cent.

items.title: NSM missile row: Malaysia awaiting Kongsberg response to demands, says Defence Minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia is waiting for Norway’s Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace (KDA) to respond to its demands after the company cancelled the export licence for Naval Strike Missiles (NSM) to Malaysia, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today. Malaysia had initially procured the NSM anti-ship missiles from KDA, but the delivery was abruptly cancelled this year despite Malaysia having settled almost 95 per cent of the contract value. Malaysia has since suspended all new defence procurements from Norway.

items.title: Kedah PKR hits out at Sanusi over remarks on gambling licences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kedah PKR has hit out at Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor for hurling insults at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim over the issue of gambling premises licences in the state. Its communications director Tunku Nashrul Abaidah said Sanusi should instead answer for his administration's defeat based on the facts and stop making the prime minister a target. "His administration's decision was overturned after the court found that it had exceeded the state's jurisdiction.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar orders immediate aid coordination following Nepal, India flood disaster
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered relevant authorities to immediately coordinate assistance following the devastating floods in Nepal and India. "I have asked all agencies, including the National Security Council and the Foreign Ministry, to immediately assess the situation and contact our embassies in India and Nepal to expedite efforts to assist those affected," he said after opening the 2026 National Innovation and Commercialisation Expo at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre today. Nepalese authorities have deployed helicopters for search-and-rescue operations, although access to some affected areas remains difficult.

items.title: [UPDATED] 'Was he invited?': Anwar rubbishes Azmin Ali's refusal to rejoin PKR
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today took a jab at former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali after the latter ruled out returning to the party. When reminded that he had spoken of welcoming otai (veterans) of the 'Reformasi' movement back into PKR, Anwar quipped: "Yes, otai. Is he (Azmin) an otai?"

items.title: High airfares force Sabahans to cancel trips, miss funerals
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Airfares between the peninsula and Sabah and Sarawak, which have surged by more than 200 per cent, are placing a growing burden on Malaysians working in the peninsula, particularly those from the B40 group. I cannot see a way for us to return to Kuala Lumpur," she said. he said.

items.title: 'Peculiar', Ismail Sabri's lawyer says of charge against ex-PM
items.summary: He raised the matter when arguing for lower bail before Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin. Amer said that the prosecution had previously filed an application under Section 41 of the MACC Act involving the same subject matter. Under Section 41, property seized under the Act may be dealt with by the court upon application by the prosecution, including cases where no prosecution is instituted.

items.title: Buloh Kasap rep Zahari Sarip sworn in as Johor state assembly Speaker
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Aug 27— Buloh Kasap assemblyman Datuk Zahari Sarip has been sworn in as the Johor state assembly Speaker following his appointment to the post. Zahari replaces Datuk Mohd Puad Zarkashi, who has held the Speaker position since the previous Johor state election in 2022. Zahari, representing Barisan Nasional (BN), successfully defended the Buloh Kasap state seat in the recent Johor state election.

items.title: FFB recovery may drive Hap Seng's second-half performance
items.summary: RHB Research said Hap Seng Plantations' second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q2 FY26) earnings were within its and consensus expectations, with first-half core earnings rising 12 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM77.7 million. On a seven-month year-to-date basis, however, FFB production rose 6.8 per cent YoY, although this remained below management's full-year growth target of 16 to 17 per cent and RHB Research's 10 per cent forecast. The firm therefore maintained its FFB production growth assumptions at 10 per cent, 5.2 per cent and 5.1 per cent for FY26 to FY28 respectively.

items.title: Nepal floods: Social media update eases sister's fears over sibling
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A sister's concern over the whereabouts and safety of her younger sibling, who is currently travelling to Annapurna Base Camp in Nepal, was eased after a social media user in the trekking area said conditions there were safe. Her concerns were eased somewhat after another Threads user, Muhammad Hafizal Hamidon, a freelance tour guide, responded to her post, saying he was currently in the Annapurna Base Camp trekking area. "I'm currently at the Annapurna Base Camp trekking area.

items.title: Malaysia tightens Thai border security, to appoint facilitators for southern Thailand peace talks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia has tightened security across its land borders with Thailand, especially across forest ranges, following recent attacks in the southern part of the country, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today. Mohamed Khaled said the armed forces are increasing surveillance at the borders to prevent insurgents from infiltrating into Malaysia and spreading the violence here. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to appoint the facilitators soon.

items.title: Shein set to raise US$1.7bil in Hong Kong IPO, sources say
items.summary: HONG KONG: Online fast-fashion retailer Shein is set to price its shares at the middle of its marketing price range to raise HK$13.6 billion (US$1.73 billion) in its Hong Kong initial public offering, according to two sources with knowledge of the matter. Shein, which is headquartered in Singapore and was founded in China, launched its long-awaited Hong Kong listing on Monday, offering 280 million shares at between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50 each. The offering is expected to be priced at HK$48.56 a share, the sources said, speaking on condition of anonymity as the information is not yet publicly available.

items.title: Defence minister: Malaysia ready to deploy humanitarian aid to flood-hit Nepal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is ready to support humanitarian missions to Nepal that is battling massive flash floods, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said today. “MAF can support humanitarian missions, if the government decides to do so, and we are ready to contribute our expertise and capabilities,” Mohamed Khaled told reporters after launching the National Day celebrations at the Defence Ministry today. However, he told reporters to refer to the Foreign Ministry for updates on the missing Malaysian tourists.

items.title: Ex-PM Ismail Sabri charged with failure to declare assets to MACC; pleads not guilty
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob was charged today with failing to declare his assets to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC). He is accused of failing to declare local and nine foreign currencies, as well as five gold bars (Suisse Fine Gold). Among the currencies allegedly not declared were RM14.7 million, S$6 million, US$1.46 million, three million Swiss francs, €12.2 million, ¥363 million, £50,250, NZ$44,600, 34.8 million dirhams and A$352,850.

items.title: More than 80 Ismail Sabri supporters travel three hours from Bera to KL court complex
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — More than 80 supporters of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob gathered outside the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex here this morning to show their support for him. Ismail Sabri, 66, who is also the Bera MP, arrived at the Sessions Court here at 8.32am to face charges under the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009. The former prime minister is expected to face a charge under Section 36(2) of the MACC Act 2009 relating to asset declaration.

items.title: Malaysia must watch the Israel –Turkey fault line in Syria closely too — Phar Kim Beng
items.summary: But Kuala Lumpur should not allow the continuing tragedy there to obscure another potentially dangerous development: the growing strategic friction between Israel and Turkey. Israel’s August 18 strikes on Syria’s Abu al-Duhur airbase in Idlib were militarily limited but strategically significant. Turkey’s expanding influence in post-Assad Syria is increasingly becoming part of Israel’s strategic calculations.

items.title: Sultan of Pahang’s sister Tengku Aishah dies, to be laid to rest with full honours
items.summary: KUANTAN, Aug 26 — The sister of the Sultan of Pahang, Tengku Puteri Seri Kemala Tengku Datuk Seri Aishah Almarhum Sultan Ahmad Shah, passed away at 9.15 pm yesterday at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur. Comptroller of the Royal Household of the Sultan of Pahang Major General Datuk Mohamed Zahari Yahya said the body of the deceased would be taken to the Pahang Royal Mausoleum, Pekan today be buried with full honours and ceremonies. He said the deceased’s death was a great loss to the Pahang Royal Family, especially to the Sultan of Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri’ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah and Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.

items.title: Ismail Sabri arrives in court to face asset declaration charges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob arrived at the Sessions Court here this morning to face charges related to his asset declaration. The 66-year-old Bera MP arrived at about 8.30am before meeting several supporters who had gathered outside the court, Kosmo! His lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad yesterday confirmed that Ismail Sabri would appear in court to face the charges.

items.title: Mohamad Hasan in Jeddah for OIC meeting on latest developments in Palestine
items.summary: JEDDAH, Aug 27 — Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan arrived here today to attend the extraordinary meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) today. He arrived at King Abdulaziz International Airport at 5.45 pm and was welcomed by Malaysian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia Datuk Syed Bakri Syed Abdul Rahman. Syed Bakri had earlier said that Malaysia’s participation in the meeting is important in conveying the country’s firm position on Israel’s actions and aggression against Palestinian territories.

items.title: Mohamad Sabu: Malaysia must leverage technology, rural development to strengthen food security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia needs to learn from China’s experience in strengthening the agricultural sector and food security through the use of technology, increased productivity and the development of rural areas that is planned in a systematic and continuous manner. Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said Malaysia has great potential to continue strengthening the country’s agro-food sector by taking appropriate approaches based on the experiences of other countries, without neglecting the interests of local industry players. “China has shown how the agricultural sector can be empowered through the use of technology, increased productivity, rural development and systematic and continuous planning.

items.title: Sulong the elephant moves into Kelantan forest after days along Gerik-Jeli highway
items.summary: Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) director-general Datuk Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said monitoring showed Sulong was no longer detected along the JRTB towards Jeli, Kosmo! He said Perhilitan personnel had been deployed to monitor the elephant’s movements and condition using drones and regular ground patrols. Department personnel have been deployed to monitor Sulong’s movements and condition using drones, as well as through regular ground monitoring,” he said.

items.title: Three foreign nationals arrested over alleged confinement of Chinese job seeker in Manjung
items.summary: Manjung district police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said the Manjung district police headquarters (IPD) operations room received a complaint from a 21-year-old victim via WhatsApp at around 10.30 pm, informing that he had been locked in the house. He said a team of police from the Manjung IPD went to the scene of the incident at around 12.15 am yesterday and arrested all three suspects, aged between 21 and 33 years, while the victim, who was suspected of being unlawfully detained, was also rescued during the raid. “The three suspects and the victim are not known to each other.

items.title: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel prices up 5 sen per litre
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will each increase by 5 sen per litre for the Aug 27 to Sept 2 period. Meanwhile, the price of subsidised RON95 under Budi Madani RON95 (BUDI95) remains at RM1.99 per litre, while subsidised diesel under Budi Madani Diesel (BUDI Diesel) remains at RM2.10 per litre. For BUDI Diesel, the subsidy borne by the government is RM2.62 per litre, or 56 per cent of the unsubsidised diesel price.

items.title: Ramanan: Malaysia to steer Asean green jobs agenda, focus on skills for future workforce
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Malaysia remains the leader of the Asean green jobs agenda for the 2026-2030 period, having been entrusted to lead regional projects related to the field under the new work programme of the Asean Labour Ministers. Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said this role was established through the Asean Labour Ministers’ Work Programme 2026-2030, thus continuing the mandate given to Malaysia in driving the green jobs agenda since chairing the Asean Labour Ministers’ Meeting (ALMM) and the Senior Labour Officials Meeting (SLOM) in 2018. Ramanan said that two important documents regarding green jobs were successfully achieved as part of the outcomes of Malaysia’s Asean Chairmanship 2025, namely the Asean Framework and Action Plan (FAP) for a Just and Inclusive Transition to Green Jobs 2025-2030 and the Joint Statement on Actionable Plan for Green Jobs Towards a Sustainable and Inclusive Asean Workforce.

items.title: Haze: Four areas in Sarawak, capital record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Three areas in Sarawak and one in Kuala Lumpur recorded Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the unhealthy range as of 7.30am today. Meanwhile, Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 129. A total of 61 monitoring stations recorded moderate readings, while two stations recorded good readings.

items.title: Anwar: Give university students full freedom to voice views, foster critical thinking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim stressed that university students must be given full freedom without restrictions that could impede their activities or prevent them from voicing their views at institutions of higher learning. Anwar said university managements and the relevant ministry must recognise that students should be given full freedom to foster a more dynamic intellectual culture. “We must accept that university students should be given full freedom without restrictions that hinder their activities.

items.title: Zambry: Comprehensive review of higher education laws needed to keep ecosystem relevant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — The future of the country’s higher education requires a comprehensive review of acts related to higher education, including the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU). Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said the move to review and improve the existing legal framework are important to ensure that the higher education ecosystem remains relevant and is not further constrained by old regulations. Meanwhile, Zambry said the Ministry of Higher Education (KPT) was also considering the drafting of a new act such as One Higher Education Act to coordinate various acts related to higher education under a more comprehensive framework.

items.title: Anwar urges patience as govt works on comprehensive AUKU reforms for students
items.summary: He said all parties need to give the government room to implement amendments or completely repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) for student freedom. “Give us room, I have fought this act (AUKU) for a long time. Also present were Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir, Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, and Academy of Sciences Malaysia President Tengku Datuk Mohd Azzman Shariffadeen.

items.title: Nepal floods: 17 Malaysians among hundreds still unaccounted for
items.summary: HYDERABAD, Aug 27 — Seventeen Malaysians are among hundreds of foreigners missing following a devastating flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district yesterday morning, according to Nepal’s tourism board. The board said in a statement that the missing Malaysians were handled by the Fishtail Tours and Travels tour agency. The Malaysian Foreign Ministry said in a statement issued earlier that 11 Malaysian nationals believed to be in Rasuwa’s district had lost contact following the flood.

items.title: Budi95’s monthly limit: How far can 200 litres take you?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 — Is 200 litres of subsidised RON95 enough to get through the month? So, how far does 200 litres go? Government data, however, shows that nearly 90 per cent of eligible Budi95 users consume less than 200 litres a month, with average monthly consumption at around 100 litres.

items.title: ‘The dream does not bode well’: Wan Junaidi recalls jungle operation that shaped his leadership
items.summary: Those were the last words uttered by Jungle Squad Constable Jabu Ajai before he was killed during an operation to hunt communist terrorists in Tulai, Sarawak, in 1971. Operation to hunt communists Recalling the incident, Wan Junaidi said that, as an Inspector at the time, he was ordered to lead his platoon to a location to conduct a special operation after a team stationed at Tulai, Binatang (now Bintangor), came under an ambush. Wan Junaidi and his men proceeded to the house for further inspection.

items.title: Anwar hails TM’s 80-year role in expanding connectivity, calls for shared prosperity
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Aug 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today praised Telekom Malaysia Bhd (TM) as an important institution in nation-building as it marked its 80th anniversary, saying the company had played a pivotal role in democratising communication across the country. Anwar, speaking at the company’s anniversary celebration here ahead of the Merdeka celebrations on Monday, said TM had evolved from its pre-independence roots into a key driver of connectivity and digital development today. Anwar said he acknowledged that TM’s privatisation helped drive corporate efficiency and profits.

items.title: Haze: Selangor local authorities told to step up monitoring, crack down on open burning
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 26 — All local authorities (PBT) in Selangor have been urged to step up monitoring to prevent open burning following unhealthy air quality recorded in several areas across the state. State Public Health and Environment Committee chairman Jamaliah Jamaluddin said the move followed the activation of the National Haze Action Plan by the Department of Environment (DOE), approved by the Selangor State Executive Council (MMKN) at its meeting today. Jamaliah also urged the public to report any open burning activities through the Selangor DOE hotline at 1-800-88-2727 or via the DOE eAduan application.
